grf.generated_hypothesis: Provider identity can be canonicalized independently from imported symbol visibility and import-cycle legality.
grf.counter_reality: A provider resolver may accidentally depend on provider list order or require a topological ordering, thereby silently minting cycle semantics.
grf.discriminator: Permute a cyclic three-package provider graph across every provider-input ordering while canonicalizing only provider identities and use modes.
grf.collapse: Provider-only binding remained order invariant in the isolated mechanism probe. This supports the phase split, but does not establish whether Clay import cycles are legal or how wildcard symbols behave.

unusual_experiment.name: CYCLIC_PROVIDER_ORDER_INVARIANCE
unusual_experiment.interpretation: A cycle need not force provider identity resolution to inherit host ordering or prematurely choose cycle legality. The result is design evidence only, not a Clay language rule.

coordination.parallel_result: PR #660 reached and merged the same provider-resolution frontier before local candidate PR #663 completed CI.
coordination.action: Closed PR #663 without merge to preserve one canonical resolver implementation.
coordination.negative_result: Independent useful work can still become architecturally harmful duplication if a parallel worker lands equivalent semantics first.
coordination.preserved_evidence: The distinct cyclic-order experiment is retained as research evidence; the duplicate code path is rejected.

external_design_evidence.finding: Go has explicit package import binding and rejects import cycles; this is not adopted as Clay semantics.
Rust resolves use declarations under its own name-resolution and glob ambiguity rules; these are not adopted as Clay semantics.

next_falsifier: Define the smallest explicit imported-symbol ownership/collision contract for MODULE versus WILDCARD uses, then prove it feeds the existing nominal checker -> ClayExecutableTypedIR/v1 -> single serialized ClayVM without bypassing the current fail-closed ClayEnv use gate until executable closure evidence exists.
